candidates.tagline: 50 years, no funding, no finish: Cape Town releases designs for its famous bridge to nowhere
candidates.story: Cape Town's Foreshore Freeway Bridge was abandoned mid-construction in 1977 when the city ran out of money; in September 2026 the city finally released its first designs for public comment — but the project still has no confirmed funding, will cost an estimated R1.8 billion, and may take another nine years to complete.
candidates.why_funny: The city built half a highway bridge in the 1970s, ran out of cash, turned the top deck into a car park for a decade, and in 2026 announced plans to finish it — with a budget of zero and a nine-year timeline.
candidates.alt: Cape Town's Foreshore Freeway Bridge photographed from street level, a dramatic concrete elevated highway that ends abruptly in mid-air above the city centre, its unfinished span jutting out with nothing beyond it against a clear blue sky

candidates.tagline: Salesforce's platform crashed during its own 40,000-person AI conference — blame: one legacy login server
candidates.story: On September 16, 2026 — Day 2 of Dreamforce, Salesforce's flagship conference with 40,000 in-person attendees — the company's entire global CRM platform went down due to a legacy login server buckling under load, locking customers out worldwide while executives were on stage unveiling AIforce and Claudeforce AI products.
candidates.why_funny: A company charging enterprise rates for AI-powered cloud reliability crashed its own flagship event because nobody had upgraded the login server — The Register noted Salesforce's $400 million annual AI budget had apparently 'gone somewhere other than their login server.'
candidates.alt: Salesforce Tower, the 61-storey tapering glass skyscraper and tallest building in San Francisco, photographed from street level against a blue sky — the headquarters of the company whose global platform collapsed during its own AI conference
